prompt: Please generate an image. Locked painterly style: hand-painted stylized game art, chunky readable shapes, detail painted not modelled, mid-level detail, softer muted colours with gentle saturation, epic and luminous, never grim. The palette's warm gold and cool teal are painted into the surfaces, but the light is flat, even studio light: no strong key light, no cast shadows, no rim light. Use the attached images only as reference as described: the first attachment is always the style reference for palette and brushwork; later attachments are the approved designs to keep. Material swatch sheet, wide landscape 16:9, plain light neutral grey background. Square swatch tiles in a neat grid, evenly spaced, each flat-on (orthographic, no perspective, no horizon, no shadows from outside the tile), a seamless tileable painterly texture with edges that would wrap, broad clumped brushwork, no tiny high-frequency noise, a short neat label under each. Swatches: Redraw of the attached reference sheet to the current spec: keep exactly the same swatches, their order and names. Old-world trim sheet, eight square tiles in a 4 x 2 grid, flat colour under even light: 1 "Pale perfect stone" (smooth near-flawless pale stone, large-block seams), 2 "Weathered pale stone" (soft stains, chips, fine cracks), 3 "Dead channel" (pale stone with the 0.5 m inset channel across it, dark empty groove with faint teal residue), 4 "Lit teal channel" (the same channel glowing soft teal), 5 "Glyph band" (a band of precise circles, arcs and lines carved into pale stone, no letters), 6 "Moss-overgrown stone", 7 "Root-cracked stone" (pale stone split by roots), 8 "Polished floor slab" (smooth pale floor with a concentric ring inlay). Title at the top: "Old world kit: materials".
